in_hebrew.name: הושענה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: הושענה הוא ביטוי עברי שמקורו בתהילים ובמזמור 'הושענה לדוד' (תהילים קיח 1-29), ופירושו 'הושע נא' או 'ישועה ה' עכשיו', והוא משמש כביטוי הלל ושבח לאלוהים, וכן הוא מופיע בברית החדשה כביטוי ששימש את הקהל היהודי בעת הכנסתו של ישוע לירושלים לפני תחילת תשוקותיו (מתי כא 9, מרקוס יא 9-10, יוחנן יב 13).

in_greek.name: Ὁσαννά
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁσαννά είναι ἡ ἑβραϊκή λέξη 'הושענה' (Hōshī‘ānāh), ἡ ὁποία ἐμφανίζεται εἰς τὸ Ψαλμὸν 118 (117) καὶ εἰς τὸν Νέον Διαθήκη, ὅταν ὁ κόσμος ἐξ ἐκκλησίας ἀπευθύνεται πρός τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὡς Μεσσίαν ἐν τῇ ἐισόδῳ αὐτοῦ εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ (Ματθαῖος 21:9, Μάρκος 11:9-10, Ἰωάννης 12:13). Ἡ λέξις σημαίνει 'Κύριος σώσον' ἤ 'Σώσον ἡμᾶς, Κύριος'.

in_latin.name: Hosanna
in_latin.long_meaning: Hosanna est vox hebraica, quae in Psalmo 118 (117) invenitur et in Novo Testamento, quando turba ecclesiastica Iesum ut Messiam in ingressu eius Hierosolymam salutavit (Matthaeus 21:9, Marcus 11:9-10, Ioannes 12:13). Vox autem significat 'Domine, salva' vel 'Salva nos, Domine'.

in_english.name: Hosanna
in_english.meaning: Save us, Lord, or Lord, save us now
in_english.long_meaning: Hosanna originates from the Hebrew expression 'הושענה' (Hōshī‘ānāh), meaning 'Save us, Lord' or 'Lord, save us now'. It appears in Psalm 118:25 and in the New Testament during Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem (Matthew 21:9, Mark 11:9-10, John 12:13). The term has become a significant expression of praise and adoration in Christian tradition, symbolizing the recognition of Jesus as the Messiah and the desire for salvation.

biblical_reference.note: Used as an expression of praise and salvation in biblical context

data.cultural_impact: In Christianity, the term "Hosanna" is most commonly associated with Palm Sunday, when crowds of people, waving palm branches and shouting "Hosanna!" welcomed Jesus into Jerusalem, believing Him to be the long-awaited Messiah come to save them from Roman rule (Matthew 21:9). Over time, this chant became a cry for salvation and deliverance from all forms of suffering.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, "Hosanna" is a powerful prayer and declaration of faith in God's saving power. It is a call for God's intervention and is rooted in the belief that God is the only true source of salvation and refuge. When we cry out "Hosanna," we are acknowledging that we cannot save ourselves and are placing our trust in God alone for deliverance and redemption. In essence, "Hosanna" is a prayer of surrender and a reminder of our dependence on God's grace and mercy.

historical_references.reference: The word 'Hosanna' comes from Hebrew, meaning 'save us, we pray'. It was a cry for help to God, especially during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. In the New Testament, it is used when the crowd greeted Jesus riding into Jerusalem, hailing Him as the 'King who comes in the name of the Lord'. (Matthew 21:9)

During the first Crusade in 1099 AD, the Crusaders entered Jerusalem and were greeted with the chanting of 'Hosanna'. This use of the word was a proclamation of their victory and recognition of God's intervention in their conquest of the city.
